topic: Hyperfocal distance: H = f^2/(N c) + f. Focus at H and everything from H/2 to infinity is acceptably sharp. 24 mm, f/8, c = 0.03 mm (full frame) gives H ~ 2.4 m, sharp from ~1.2 m; at f/16, H ~ 1.2 m
lines: Focus on the horizon, and your foreground goes soft.
Depth of field is the zone that looks acceptably sharp. Focus on infinity, and that zone starts too far away.
Focus instead at the hyperfocal distance. Everything from half that distance to infinity is acceptably sharp.
The formula: focal length squared, divided by f-number times circle of confusion, plus focal length.
A twenty-four millimetre lens at f eight on full frame, with the usual zero point zero three millimetre circle of confusion, gives about two point four metres.
A 24 mm lens at f/8 on full frame, with the usual 0.03 mm circle of confusion, gives about 2.4 metres.
Focus there, and everything from about one point two metres to infinity is acceptably sharp.
Focus there, and everything from about 1.2 metres to infinity is acceptably sharp.
Stop down to f sixteen, and the distance drops to about one point two metres.
Stop down to f/16, and the distance drops to about 1.2 metres.
Don't focus on the horizon. Focus on the hyperfocal distance.

youtube.title: Stop Focusing on the Horizon: Use Hyperfocal Distance
youtube.description:
The hyperfocal distance is H = f²/(N·c) + f (f = focal length, N = f-number, c = circle of confusion). If you focus at H, everything from H/2 to infinity is acceptably sharp, so you get more sharp foreground than by focusing on infinity. Example: a 24 mm lens at f/8 on full frame with c = 0.03 mm gives H ≈ 2.4 m, so about 1.2 m to infinity is acceptably sharp; at f/16, H ≈ 1.2 m. 'Acceptably sharp' depends on c and on how large you view the image. The landscape is a simulation (thin-lens defocus, 100% crop), not a real photo.

sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperfocal_distance (H = f^2/(N c) + f; focusing at H gives acceptable sharpness from H/2 to infinity; worked example 50 mm f/8 c = 0.03 mm -> ~10.5 m, sharp from ~5.2 m; c = 0.03 mm typical for 35 mm photography)

Simulation: thin-lens blur b = f^2/(N(s-f)) x |d-s|/d; at s = H the near limit H/2 and infinity both give b = c = 0.03 mm; focus at infinity gives b = 0.06 mm at 1.2 m. Layers at 1.2 m, 5 m, infinity; shown as a 100% crop (1 px = 0.006 mm).
